common_name: Icicles Licorice Plant (Curly Silver Needle Foliage)

planting.note: Set out rooted cuttings or nursery starts once the danger of frost has passed; the twisted, wiry foliage benefits from a lean, fast-draining mix that mimics its native dry-slope habitat.

directions: Give this selection full sun and gritty, well-drained soil, since its thin, curled, silvery-white leaves are prone to rot if kept wet or shaded. Unlike the broad, felted leaves of common licorice plant, 'Icicles' produces fine, twisting, almost wire-like foliage that adds a spiky, textural contrast at the edge of containers and rock gardens. It tolerates heat and drought well once established and rarely needs deadheading, since its small yellow flower clusters are secondary to the foliage display. Shear lightly in midsummer if growth becomes leggy to keep the curled texture dense.

common_name: Silver Mist Licorice Plant (Compact Mounding Silver Foliage)

planting.note: Set out rooted cuttings or nursery starts after all danger of frost; this compact, well-branched selection fills in quickly in average, well-drained container mix.

directions: Plant in full sun and moderately fertile, well-drained soil for the softest, most silvery leaf color; part shade shifts the foliage toward green. 'Silver Mist' branches more densely than the species, forming a tidy mounding-to-trailing plant with fuzzy, oval, felted leaves that soften and unify bold flower colors in mixed plantings. It is drought tolerant once established and benefits from an occasional pinch to keep the mound compact through the season. Small cream flower spikes appear in late summer but are incidental to its use as a foliage filler.

common_name: White Licorice Plant (Velvety Silver-White Trailing Foliage)

planting.note: Set out nursery starts or rooted cuttings once nights stay reliably above 50°F; a Proven Accents selection valued for its intensely white, velvety leaf color in combination plantings.

directions: Grow in full sun to part sun and well-drained soil; this selection carries a heavier coat of white wool than the species, giving it a brighter, almost frosted appearance that holds up well in heat. It is vigorous and low-maintenance, requiring little feeding to stay full through the season, and pairs especially well as a color-cooling filler against bold reds and purples. Trim trailing stems back by a third if they become sparse at the base to encourage fresh branching. Established plants shrug off heat and short dry spells but look best with consistent container moisture.

common_name: Petite Licorice Plant (Dwarf Compact Silver Foliage)

planting.note: Set out rooted cuttings or nursery starts after the last frost; its small, dense leaves make it well suited to compact combination pots where a full-sized licorice plant would overwhelm neighboring plants.

directions: Plant in full to part sun in well-drained soil; the dwarf, densely felted leaves stay proportionally small even as the plant matures, making it useful along the rim of smaller pots or window boxes rather than the sprawling hanging baskets suited to standard licorice plant. It tolerates heat, wind, and salt exposure well once rooted in and needs no deadheading. Light shearing keeps the sprawling stems from opening up in the center of the plant. Water when the top inch of soil dries, as it resents constantly soggy conditions.
sources: North Shore Plant Club plant database

common_name: Goldilocks Creeping Jenny (Glossy Golden Trailing Groundcover)

planting.note: Divide or set out rooted sections in spring once the soil is workable; establishes readily in consistently moist soil and spreads by rooting at the stem nodes.

directions: Plant in moist to consistently damp soil in partial shade to full sun, adjusting exposure so the rounded leaves stay glossy gold rather than scorching in harsh afternoon heat. 'Goldilocks' holds a brighter, more saturated yellow color through the season than older golden selections and forms a tight, fast-knitting mat useful for edging paths, softening container rims, or covering damp low spots. Small yellow cup-shaped flowers appear in the leaf axils in early summer but are secondary to the foliage display. Shear back hard if it spreads beyond its bounds, since like other creeping Jenny selections it roots wherever stems touch soil.

common_name: Outback Sunset Loosestrife (Gold-and-Green Variegated Trailing Foliage)

planting.note: Set out rooted cuttings or nursery starts after frost danger passes; grown as a fast-filling annual trailer outside its hardy range and as a spreading groundcover within it.

directions: Plant in evenly moist, well-drained soil in part sun to part shade, where the oval leaves develop their signature gold-and-green pattern most vividly. Compact, red-centered yellow flowers appear scattered across the mat in spring and summer, adding a warm accent to the variegated foliage below. This selection trails eagerly over container edges and walls but is far less aggressive as a spreader than plain creeping Jenny, making it manageable in smaller planters. Feed lightly through the growing season and pinch stem tips to keep the mat dense rather than sparse and vining.
